elements.name: Beispielarchitektur
elements.notes: Architektur Projektarchitektur -- aus dem Regelwerk erzeugtes Geruest.

elements.name: Startseite Projektarchitektur
elements.notes: Startansicht des Modells.

elements.name: A1 - Meta-Data Definitions
elements.notes: Architectures, particularly large ones, usually require meta-data tags to aid with searching and discovery.

elements.name: Meta-Data Definitions
elements.notes: Sicht A1 - Meta-Data Definitions.

elements.name: A2 - Architecture Products
elements.notes: The A2 Viewpoint specifies the structure of an architecture, and the products that describe the architecture. Each product may correspond to an architecture view. This viewpoint also traces the architectures onto the Enterprise Phases they correspond to (see also C2 – Enterprise Vision) and identifies the key stakeholders, their concerns and the products that address those concerns (from ISO/IEC/IEEE Standards).

elements.name: Architecture Products
elements.notes: Sicht A2 - Architecture Products.

elements.name: A3 - Architecture Correspondence
elements.notes: ISO/IEC/IEEE42010 introduces the idea of architecture correspondence and correspondence rules. Quoting from ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010; “A correspondence defines a relation between AD (Architecture Description) elements. Correspondences are used to express architecture relations of interest within an architecture description (or between architecture descriptions). Correspondences can be governed by correspondence rules. Correspondence rules are used to enforce relations within an architecture description (or between architecture descriptions).”

elements.name: Architecture Correspondence
elements.notes: Sicht A3 - Architecture Correspondence.

elements.name: A4 - Methodology Used
elements.notes: The A4 Viewpoint specifies the methodology used for the architecting activities. This methodology is described in NAFv4 Chapter 2. The content of the A4 viewpoint can also be modeled in the A1 viewpoint.

elements.name: Methodology Used
elements.notes: Sicht A4 - Methodology Used.

elements.name: A5 - Architecture Status
elements.notes: Since NAFv3.0, it has been possible to assign version numbers to views and specify their approval dates. In NAFv4.0, this is integrated with the meta-model’s generic project and milestone approach so that architecture releases are tracked against the architecture delivery project. The content of the A5 viewpoint can also be modeled in the A1 viewpoint.

elements.name: Architecture Status
elements.notes: Sicht A5 - Architecture Status.

elements.name: A6 - Architecture Version
elements.notes: Where the A5 Viewpoint shows the current version number and approval status for the architecture, the A6 Viewpoint shows the complete history of the architecture.

elements.name: Architecture Version
elements.notes: Sicht A6 - Architecture Version.

elements.name: A7 - Architecture Compliance
elements.notes: The A7 Viewpoint gives the overall specification of architecture meta-data.

elements.name: Architecture Compliance
elements.notes: Sicht A7 - Architecture Compliance.

elements.name: A8 - Standards
elements.notes: The A8 Viewpoint encompasses both technical and non-technical standards. The standards specified in the A8 view can be applied across the architecture to a variety of structural and behavioural elements. Standards are essential to the coherent running of businesses and to the delivery of reliable, interoperable systems.

elements.name: Standards
elements.notes: Sicht A8 - Standards.

elements.name: Ar - Architecture Roadmap
elements.notes: The Ar Viewpoint shows the history of the architecture project as well as its future direction.

elements.name: Architecture Roadmap
elements.notes: Sicht Ar - Architecture Roadmap.

elements.name: C1 - Capability Taxonomy
elements.notes: The C1 Viewpoint specifies all the capabilities that are referenced throughout one or more architectures – i.e. one C1 may provide the definitive list of capabilities for a number of logical and resource architectures. The capabilities may be organised into specialisation hierarchies (taxonomies). Measures of Effectiveness (MoE) may be specified for each capability. Note that MoEs are inherited down a capability taxonomy.

elements.name: Capability Taxonomy
elements.notes: Sicht C1 - Capability Taxonomy.

elements.name: C2 - Enterprise Vision
elements.notes: The purpose of the C2 Viewpoint is to provide a strategic context for the capabilities described in the architecture and to specify the scope for the architecture. The C2 Viewpoint is high-level and describes the vision, goals, enduring tasks and capabilities using terminology that is easily understood by non-technical readers.

elements.name: Enterprise Vision
elements.notes: Sicht C2 - Enterprise Vision.

elements.name: C3 - Capability Dependencies
elements.notes: The C3 Viewpoint is intended to provide a means of analysing the dependencies between capabilities and between capability clusters. The composition of capabilities (into clusters) is logical and the purpose of the clusters is to guide enterprise management.

elements.name: Capability Dependencies
elements.notes: Sicht C3 - Capability Dependencies.

elements.name: C4 - Standard Processes
elements.notes: The C4 Viewpoint specifies Standard Operational Activities that can be re-used across multiple logical architectures (e.g. in L4, Logical Activities).

elements.name: Standard Processes
elements.notes: Sicht C4 - Standard Processes.

elements.name: C5 - Effects
elements.notes: The purpose of the C5 Viewpoint is to describe the operational effect of the capabilities, activities and services according to the expected goals. The C5 Viewpoint is high-level description that should be easily understood by non-technical readers.

elements.name: Effects
elements.notes: Sicht C5 - Effects.

elements.name: C7 - Performance Parameters
elements.notes: In the C7 Viewpoint the capability requirements (and existing capabilities) can be expressed in terms of Measures of Effectiveness (MoEs). These are high-level metrics used to judge the level of capability.

elements.name: Performance Parameters
elements.notes: Sicht C7 - Performance Parameters.

elements.name: C8 - Planning Assumptions
elements.notes: The C8 Viewpoint is concerned with identification and description of assumptions that have been made for the implementation of capabilities. Assumptions can be expressed by means of requirements.

elements.name: Planning Assumptions
elements.notes: Sicht C8 - Planning Assumptions.

elements.name: Cr - Capability Roadmap
elements.notes: The Cr Viewpont supports the Capability Audit process by providing a method to identify gaps or duplications in capability provision. Cr indicates capability increments, which are derived from delivery milestones within acquisition projects.

elements.name: Capability Roadmap
elements.notes: Sicht Cr - Capability Roadmap.

elements.name: L1 - Node Types
elements.notes: The L1 Viewpoint defines all of the Nodes that will appear in a Logical Architecture. Nodes are elements of capability assembled and orchestrated in the Logical Architecture (see L2 - Logical Scenario and L4 - Logical Activities views). The levels of capability provided by each node are expressed as Measures of Performance (MoPs) and these may be dependent on the environments in which the Node is required to operate.

elements.name: Node Types
elements.notes: Sicht L1 - Node Types.

elements.name: L2 - Logical Scenario
elements.notes: The L2 Viewpoint specifies Nodes (elements of capability) in context of each other. The context is usually expressed in terms of the information that flows between the nodes (e.g. the information flow requirements between capabilities in a given scenario) but may also be flows of materiel, human resource or energy.

elements.name: Logical Scenario
elements.notes: Sicht L2 - Logical Scenario.

elements.name: L2-L3 - Logical Concept
elements.notes: The L2-L3 Viewpoint is concerned with providing an executive level, scenario-based communication of the architecture purpose, scope and content.

elements.name: Logical Concept
elements.notes: Sicht L2-L3 - Logical Concept.

elements.name: L3 - Node Interactions
elements.notes: L3 is used to provide further detail of the interoperability requirements associated with the operational capability of interest. The focus is on logical flows that cross the capability boundary. Although the primary purpose of the L3 Viewpoint is to specify information exchanges, the L3 may also list flows of materiel, energy and human resources.

elements.name: Node Interactions
elements.notes: Sicht L3 - Node Interactions.

elements.name: L4 - Logical Activities
elements.notes: The L4 Viewpoint describes the operational activities that are being conducted within the mission or scenario. These activities are defined at a logical, solution-neutral level so as to enable different solutions in the physical layer. The L4 Viewpoint describes the activities associated with the logical architecture, as well as the:

elements.name: Logical Activities
elements.notes: Sicht L4 - Logical Activities.

elements.name: L5 - Logical States
elements.notes: The L5 Viewpoint specifies the typical states a node may have and the possible transitions between those states (i.e. changes of state). Triggers for state changes may also be defined. Actions may be associated with a given state or with the transition between states in response to stimuli (e.g. triggers and events).

elements.name: Logical States
elements.notes: Sicht L5 - Logical States.

elements.name: L6 - Logical Sequence
elements.notes: Operational Event-Trace Descriptions, sometimes called sequence diagrams, event scenarios or timing diagrams, allow the tracing of interactions between nodes in a scenario or critical sequence of events. The node interactions usually correspond to flows of information but may describe flows of energy, materiel or people specified in the L2, Logical Scenario.

elements.name: Logical Sequence
elements.notes: Sicht L6 - Logical Sequence.

elements.name: L7 - Information Model
elements.notes: The L7 Viewpoint is used to document the business information. It describes the information that can be exchanged along the logical flows in the architecture, specified in L3 Node Interactions.

elements.name: Information Model
elements.notes: Sicht L7 - Information Model.

elements.name: L8 - Logical Constraints
elements.notes: The L8 Viewpoint is used to constrain the logical architecture without forcing a particular solution. L8 is used for rules which are not expressed as behavioural models, interactions or measures of effectiveness, i.e. they are textual statements of requirements that constrain the architecture.

elements.name: Logical Constraints
elements.notes: Sicht L8 - Logical Constraints.

elements.name: Lr - Lines of Development
elements.notes: The Lr Viewpoint is primarily intended to support the acquisition process across multiple projects or programmes, highlighting dependencies the logical dependencies between capabilities, projects and the integration of all lines of development to achieve a successfully integrated military capability. Use of the Lr Viewpoint should support the management of capability delivery and be aligned with Cr, Capability Roadmap.

elements.name: Lines of Development
elements.notes: Sicht Lr - Lines of Development.

elements.name: C1-S1 - Capability to Service Mapping
elements.notes: A C1-S1 Viewpoint presents a simple mapping of services to capabilities, showing which services contribute to which capability.

elements.name: Capability to Service Mapping
elements.notes: Sicht C1-S1 - Capability to Service Mapping.

elements.name: S1 - Service Taxonomy
elements.notes: The purpose of the S1 Viewpoint is to provide a governance structure for a Service-Oriented Architecture. Along with S3, Service Interfaces, it specifies a standard library of service specifications for an enterprise, to which service implementers are expected to conform.

elements.name: Service Taxonomy
elements.notes: Sicht S1 - Service Taxonomy.

elements.name: S2 - Service Structure
elements.notes: The S2 Viewpoint is concerned with identification and description of how services are structured to create a higher-aggregated service. To provide highlevel views, dependencies to other services, nodes and resources as well as service interfaces and service functions can be represented.

elements.name: Service Structure
elements.notes: Sicht S2 - Service Structure.

elements.name: S3 - Service Interfaces
elements.notes: The S3 Viewpoint is concerned with the identification and definition of service interfaces.

elements.name: Service Interfaces
elements.notes: Sicht S3 - Service Interfaces.

elements.name: S4 - Service Functions
elements.notes: The S4 Viewpoint is the key behavioural specification for services. Equivalent in nature to L4, Logical Activities and P4, Resources Functions, it specifies a set of functions that a service implementation is expected to perform. Implementation of that behaviour is represented in P4, Resource Functions, and L4-P4, Activity to Function Mapping.

elements.name: Service Functions
elements.notes: Sicht S4 - Service Functions.

elements.name: S5 - Service States
elements.notes: The S5 Viewpoint is a specification of the allowable states of a service, and the possible transitions between them. This specification constrains how implementations of the service will behave.  It is, though, generally considered a good practice to make services stateless - i.e. consumers of a service are not aware of what state the service is in.

elements.name: Service States
elements.notes: Sicht S5 - Service States.

elements.name: S6 - Service Interactions
elements.notes: Service Interaction Descriptions, sometimes called sequence diagrams, event scenarios or timing diagrams, allow the tracing of interactions between services in a composition or critical sequence of events.

elements.name: Service Interactions
elements.notes: Sicht S6 - Service Interactions.

elements.name: S7 - Service Interface Parameters
elements.notes: Specifies the interfaces that a service provides and uses, defines which services are compatible with which other services.

elements.name: Service Interface Parameters
elements.notes: Sicht S7 - Service Interface Parameters.

elements.name: S8 - Service Policy
elements.notes: The S8 Viewpoint specifies constraints against services to which implementations must conform.

elements.name: Service Policy
elements.notes: Sicht S8 - Service Policy.

elements.name: Sr - Service Roadmap
elements.notes: The Sr Viewpoint supports the Service Audit process by providing a method to identify gaps or duplications in service provision. Sr indicates service lifetime evolutions, which are derived from delivery milestones within acquisition projects.

elements.name: Service Roadmap
elements.notes: Sicht Sr - Service Roadmap.

elements.name: P1 - Resource Types
elements.notes: The P1 Viewpoint collects together all the Resource Types in the architecture together with a depiction of their performance characteristics. P1 also provides a summary of the technologies and competencies that impact on the Resources that constitute the architecture.

elements.name: Resource Types
elements.notes: Sicht P1 - Resource Types.

elements.name: P2 - Resource Structure
elements.notes: The P2 Viewpoint links together the operational and physical architecture viewpoints by depicting how types of Resource are structured and interact to realize the logical architecture specified in L2, Logical Scenario. The P2 Viewpoint may represent the realization of a requirement specified in a L2 (i.e. in a “to-be” architecture) and so there may be many alternative Resource viewpoint suites that could realize the operational requirement. Alternatively, in an “as-is” architecture, a L2 may just be a simplified, logical representation of the P2 Viewpoint to allow communication of key information flows to non-technical stakeholders.

elements.name: Resource Structure
elements.notes: Sicht P2 - Resource Structure.

elements.name: P3 - Resource Connectivity
elements.notes: The networks and pathways documented in a P3 Viewpoint represent the physical implementation of the logical flows identified in a L2, Logical Scenario, or L3, Node Interactions View.

elements.name: Resource Connectivity
elements.notes: Sicht P3 - Resource Connectivity.

elements.name: P4 - Resource Functions
elements.notes: The Functionality Description provides detailed information regarding the allocation of functions to resources, and flows between Resource Functions. The P4 Viewpoint is the Physical Resource counterpart to the L4 Logical Activities Viewpoint.

elements.name: Resource Functions
elements.notes: Sicht P4 - Resource Functions.

elements.name: P5 - Resource States
elements.notes: The P5 Viewpoint identifies the states a Resource can be, the allowable changes between those states, and the stimuli (e.g. triggers and events) that cause the state changes.

elements.name: Resource States
elements.notes: Sicht P5 - Resource States.

elements.name: P6 - Resource Sequence
elements.notes: The P6 Viewpoint is valuable for moving to the next level of detail from the initial solution design, to help define a sequence of functions and Resource Interactions, and to ensure that each participating Resource or Port has the necessary information, at the right time, in order to perform its assigned functionality.

elements.name: Resource Sequence
elements.notes: Sicht P6 - Resource Sequence.

elements.name: P7 - Data Model
elements.notes: The P7 Viewpoint is one of the architectural products closest to actual system design in the NAF. It is used to describe how the information represented in the L7 Logical Data Model Viewpoint is implemented.

elements.name: Data Model
elements.notes: Sicht P7 - Data Model.

elements.name: P8 - Resource Constraints
elements.notes: The P8 Viewpoint describes constraints on the Resources, Resource Functions, data and communications that make up a Physical Architecture.

elements.name: Resource Constraints
elements.notes: Sicht P8 - Resource Constraints.

elements.name: Pr - Configuration Management
elements.notes: The Pr Viewpoint provides an overview of how Resource Assets change over time (note that NAF v3.1 only allowed for Capability Configurations whereas now this is opened up to all Resource Types). It shows the structure of different versions of Resource Assets (usually Capability Configurations or Service Implementations) mapped against a timeline.

elements.name: Configuration Management
elements.notes: Sicht Pr - Configuration Management.

elements.name: L4-P4 - Activity To Function Mapping
elements.notes: The L4-P4 Viewpoint depicts the mapping of Resource Functions (and optionally, the resources that provide them) to operational activities and/or service functions. For operational activities it thus identifies the transformation of an operational need into a purposeful action performed by a system or solution. For service functions it provides the link between the services used at the operational level and the specific Resource Functions provided by the resources supporting the services.

elements.name: Activity To Function Mapping
elements.notes: Sicht L4-P4 - Activity To Function Mapping.

elements.name: R2 - Requirement Catalogue
elements.notes: The R2 represents a catalog of requirements in the architectural model. For this purpose, categories can be created in which the functional and non-functional requirements can be grouped.

elements.name: Requirement Catalogue
elements.notes: Sicht R2 - Requirement Catalogue.

elements.name: R3 - Requirement Dependencies
elements.notes: The R3 is used to show dependencies between different requirements.

elements.name: Requirement Dependencies
elements.notes: Sicht R3 - Requirement Dependencies.

elements.name: R7 - Requirement Derivation
elements.notes: The R7 assigns functional and non-functional requirements to the demanding architectural elements. In addition, information about the planned realization can be shown.

elements.name: Requirement Derivation
elements.notes: Sicht R7 - Requirement Derivation.

elements.name: R8 - Requirement Fulfilment
elements.notes: The R8 is used to determine and map acceptance and evaluation criteria for the individual functional and non-functional requirements.

elements.name: Requirement Fulfilment
elements.notes: Sicht R8 - Requirement Fulfilment.

elements.name: Rr - Requirement Realization
elements.notes: In the Rr, requirements are assigned to the realizing architectural elements.

elements.name: Requirement Realization
elements.notes: Sicht Rr - Requirement Realization.

elements.name: Achiever
elements.notes: An ActualResource, ActualProject or ActualEnterprisePhase that can deliver a DesiredEffect.

elements.name: ActualCondition
elements.notes: An individual describing an actual situation with respect to circumstances under which an OperationalActivity, Function or ServiceFunction can be performed.

elements.name: ActualEnduringTask
elements.notes: An actual undertaking recognized by an enterprise as being essential to achieving its goals - i.e. a strategic specification of what the enterprise does.

elements.name: ActualEnterprisePhase
elements.notes: The ActualState that describes the phase of an Enterprise endeavor.

elements.name: ActualEnvironment
elements.notes: The ActualState that describes the circumstances of an Environment.

elements.name: ActualLocation
elements.notes: The ActualState that describes a physical location, for example using text to provide an address, Geo-coordinates, etc.

elements.name: ActualMeasurement
elements.notes: An actual value that is applied to a Measurement.

elements.name: ActualMeasurementSet
elements.notes: A set of ActualMeasurements.

elements.name: ActualOrganization
elements.notes: An actual formal or informal organizational unit, e.g. "Driving and Vehicle Licensing Agency", "UAF team Alpha".

elements.name: ActualOrganizationalResource
elements.notes: Abstract element for an ActualOrganization, ActualPerson or ActualPost.

elements.name: ActualOrganizationRole
elements.notes: An ActualOrganizationalResource that is applied to a ResourceRole.

elements.name: ActualPerson
elements.notes: An individual human being.

elements.name: ActualPost
elements.notes: An actual, specific post, an instance of a Post "type" - e.g., "President of the United States of America." where the Post would be president.

elements.name: ActualProject
elements.notes: A time-limited endeavor to provide a specific set of ActualResource that meet specific Capability needs.

elements.name: ActualProjectMilestone
elements.notes: An event with a start date in a ActualProject from which progress is measured.

elements.name: ActualProjectMilestoneRole
elements.notes: An ActualProjectMilestone that is applied to a ProjectMilestoneRole.

elements.name: ActualPropertySet
elements.notes: A set or collection of Actual properties.

elements.name: ActualResource
elements.notes: Role in an Organisation, where the role carries the authority to undertake a function - through the ActualOrganizationalResource given the role has the responsibility.

elements.name: ActualResourceRole
elements.notes: An instance of a ResourcePerformer.

elements.name: ActualResponsibleResource
elements.notes: An abstract type grouping responsible OrganizationalResources.

elements.name: ActualService
elements.notes: An individual ServiceSpecification.

elements.name: ActualServiceSpecificationRole
elements.notes: An instance of a ServiceSpecification in context of a ServiceSpecification.

elements.name: ActualState
elements.notes: Abstract element that applies temporal extent to a set of elements realized as Instance Specifications.

elements.name: Architecture
elements.notes: An abstract type that represents a generic architecture. Subtypes are OperationalArchitecture and ResourceArchitecture.

elements.name: Asset
elements.notes: Asset as applied to Security views, an abstract type that indicates the types of elements that can be considered as a subject for security analysis.

elements.name: AssetRole
elements.notes: AssetRole as applied to Security views, an abstract element that indicates the type of elements  that can be considered as a subject for security analysis in the particular context (currently no security viewpoints in the framework).

elements.name: BusinessProcess
elements.notes: An abstract type that represents a behavior or process (i.e. a Function or OperationalActivity) that can be performed by a Performer.

elements.name: BWRequirement
elements.notes: Abstract base class for requirements.

elements.name: Capability
elements.notes: A high level specification of the enterprise's ability to execute a specified course of action.

elements.name: CapabilityConfiguration
elements.notes: A composite structure representing the physical and human resources (and their interactions) in an enterprise, assembled to meet a capability).

elements.name: CapabilityRole
elements.notes: A high level specification of the enterprise's ability to execute a specified course of action.

elements.name: Classification
elements.notes: Classification according to STANAG 1059.

elements.name: Competence
elements.notes: A specific set of abilities defined by knowledge, skills and aptitude.

elements.name: ConceptRole
elements.notes: Usage of a ConceptItem in the context of a HighLevelOperationalConcept.

elements.name: Concern
elements.notes: Interest in an EnterprisePhase (EnterprisePhase is synonym for System in ISO 42010) relevant to one or more of its stakeholders.

elements.name: Condition
elements.notes: A type that defines the Location, Environment and/or GeoPoliticalExtent.

elements.name: DataElement
elements.notes: A formalized representation of data that is managed by or exchanged between resources.

elements.name: DataRole
elements.notes: A usage of DataElement that exists in the context of an ResourceAsset. It also allows the representation of the whole-part aggregation of DataElements.

elements.name: DocumentReference
elements.notes: The element describes a regulation, instruction or a general document.

elements.name: EnduringTask
elements.notes: A type of template behavior recognized by an enterprise as being essential to achieving its goals - i.e. a template for a strategic specification of what the enterprise does.

elements.name: Energy
elements.notes: A representation of any kind of energy.

elements.name: EnterpriseGoal
elements.notes: A statement about a state or condition of the enterprise to be brought about or sustained through appropriate Means. An EnterpriseGoal amplifies an EnterpriseVision that is, it indicates what must be satisfied on a continuing basis to effectively attain the EnterpriseVision.

elements.name: EnterprisePhase
elements.notes: A current or future state of the wholeLifeEnterprise or another EnterprisePhase.

elements.name: EnterpriseVision
elements.notes: A Vision describes the future state of the enterprise, without regard to how it is to be achieved.

elements.name: Environment
elements.notes: A definition of the environmental factors in which something exists or functions. The definition of an Environment element can be further defined using EnvironmentKind.

elements.name: EnvironmentProperty
elements.notes: A property of an Environment that is typed by a Condition.  The kinds of Condition that can be represented are Location, GeoPoliticalExtentType and Environment.

elements.name: FieldedCapability
elements.notes: An individual, fully-realized capability.

elements.name: Finding
elements.notes: An ascertainment made in the model, which relates to the methodology used, the subject under consideration, the tool or something else.

elements.name: FitCriterion
elements.notes: This element represents an acceptance criterion for a functional or non-functional requirement.

elements.name: FulfilmentCriterion
elements.notes: This element represents a criterion for evaluating the degree of implementation of a functional or non-functional requirement.

elements.name: Function
elements.notes: An Activity which is specified in the context to the ResourcePerformer (human or machine) that IsCapableToPerform it.

elements.name: FunctionAction
elements.notes: A call of a Function indicating that the Function is performed by a ResourceRole in a specific context.

elements.name: FunctionalRequirement
elements.notes: The element represents a functional requirement (what should the system / software be able to do?).

elements.name: GeoPoliticalExtentType
elements.notes: A geospatial extent whose boundaries are defined by declaration or agreement by political parties.

elements.name: HighLevelOperationalConcept
elements.notes: Describes the Resources and Locations required to meet an operational scenario from an integrated systems point of view. It is used to communicate overall quantitative and qualitative system characteristics to stakeholders

elements.name: InformationElement
elements.notes: An item of information that flows between OperationalPerformers and is produced and consumed by the OperationalActivities that the OperationalPerformers are capable to perform (see IsCapableToPerform).

elements.name: InformationRole
elements.notes: A usage of InformationElement that exists in the context of an OperationalAsset. It also allows the representation of the whole-part aggregation of InformationElements.

elements.name: InteractionRole
elements.notes: An abstract type that represents an individual participant in the InteractionScenario.

elements.name: KnownResource
elements.notes: Asserts that a known ResourcePerformer constrains the implementation of the OperationalPerformer that plays the role in the LogicalArchitecture.

elements.name: Location
elements.notes: A specification of the generic area in which a LocationHolder is required to be located.

elements.name: Measurement
elements.notes: A property of an element representing something in the physical world, expressed in amounts of a unit of measure.

elements.name: MeasurementType
elements.notes: A type of a property representing something in the physical world, expressed in amounts of a unit of measure.

elements.name: NaturalResource
elements.notes: Type of physical resource that occurs in nature.

elements.name: NonfunctionalRequirement
elements.notes: The element represents a non-functional requirement (how should the system / software be able to do something?).

elements.name: OperationalActivity
elements.notes: An Activity that captures a logical process, specified independently of how the process is carried out.

elements.name: OperationalActivityAction
elements.notes: A call of an OperationalActivity in the context of another OperationalActivity.

elements.name: OperationalAgent
elements.notes: An abstract type grouping Operational Architecture and Operational Performer.

elements.name: OperationalArchitecture
elements.notes: A type used to denote a model of the Architecture, described from the Operational perspective.

elements.name: OperationalAsset
elements.notes: An abstract element used to group the elements of OperationalAgent and InformationElement allowing them to own InformationRoles.

elements.name: OperationalConstraint
elements.notes: A Rule governing a logical architectural element i.e. OperationalPerformer, OperationalActivity, InformationElement etc.

elements.name: OperationalInterface
elements.notes: A declaration that specifies a contract between the OperationalPerformer it is related to, and any other OperationalPerformers it can interact with.

elements.name: OperationalMethod
elements.notes: behavioral feature of a OperationalPerformer whose behavior is specified in an OperationalActivity.

elements.name: OperationalParameter
elements.notes: A type that represents inputs and outputs of an OperationalActivity. It is typed by an OperationalExchangeItem.

elements.name: OperationalPerformer
elements.notes: A logical entity that IsCapableToPerform OperationalActivities which produce, consume and process Resources.

elements.name: OperationalPort
elements.notes: An interaction point for an OperationalAgent through which it can interact with the outside environment and which is defined by an OperationalInterface.

elements.name: OperationalRole
elements.notes: Usage of a OperationalPerformer or OperationalArchitecture in the context of another OperationalPerformer or OperationalArchitecture. Creates a whole-part relationship.

elements.name: OperationalSignal
elements.notes: An item of information that flows between OperationalPerformers and is produced and consumed by the OperationalActivities that the OperationalPerformers are capable of performing (see IsCapableToPerform).

elements.name: OperationalSignalProperty
elements.notes: A property of an OperationalSignal typed by OperationalExchangeItem. It enables OperationalExchangeItem e.g. InformationElement to be passed as arguments of the OperationalSignal.

elements.name: OperationalStateDescription
elements.notes: A state machine describing the behavior of a OperationalPerformer, depicting how the OperationalPerformer responds to various events and the actions.

elements.name: Organization
elements.notes: A group of OrganizationalResources (Persons, Posts, Organizations and Responsibilities) associated for a particular purpose.

elements.name: OrganizationalResource
elements.notes: An abstract type for Organization, Person Post and Responsibility.

elements.name: PaperForm
elements.notes: Form is a digitized or digitizable document, for example a scanned document.

elements.name: Person
elements.notes: A type of a human being used to define the characteristics that need to be described for ActualPersons (e.g. properties such as address, telephone number, nationality, etc).

elements.name: PhysicalResource
elements.notes: An abstract type defining physical resources (i.e. OrganizationalResource, ResourceArtifact and NaturalResource).

elements.name: Post
elements.notes: A type of job title or position that a person can fill (e.g. Lawyer, Solution Architect, Machine Operator or Chief Executive Officer).

elements.name: PostRole
elements.notes: A usage of a post in the context of another OrganizationalResource. Creates a whole-part relationship.

elements.name: ProblemDomain
elements.notes: A property associated with a logical architecture, used to specify the scope of the problem.

elements.name: Project
elements.notes: A type that describes types of time-limited endeavours that are required to meet one or more Capability needs.

elements.name: ProjectMilestone
elements.notes: A type of event in a Project by which progress is measured.

elements.name: ProjectMilestoneRole
elements.notes: The role played by a ProjectMilestone in the context of a Project.

elements.name: ProjectRole
elements.notes: Usage of a Project in the context of another Project. Creates a whole-part relationship.

elements.name: ProjectStatus
elements.notes: The status (i.e. level of progress) of a ProjectTheme for an ActualProject at the time of the ActualProjectMilestone.

elements.name: ProjectTheme
elements.notes: A property of a ProjectMilestone that captures an aspect by which the progress of ActualProjects may be measured.

elements.name: Protocol
elements.notes: A Standard for communication over a network. Protocols may be composite, represented as a ProtocolStack made up of ProtocolLayers.

elements.name: ProtocolLayer
elements.notes: Usage of a Protocol in the context of another Protocol. Creates a whole-part relationship.

elements.name: Protocolstack
elements.notes: A sub type of Protocol that contains the ProtocolLayers, defining a complete stack.

elements.name: ProvidedServiceLevel
elements.notes: A sub type of ActualService that details a specific service level delivered by the provider.

elements.name: Recommendation
elements.notes: Need for action from a finding.

elements.name: Reference
elements.notes: Element describes all types of references.

elements.name: RequiredServiceLevel
elements.notes: A sub type of ActualService that details a specific service level required of the provider.

elements.name: RequirementCatalogue
elements.notes: Element represents a catalog of requirements, which consists of different categories (RequirementCategory) of functional and non-functional requirements.

elements.name: RequirementCategory
elements.notes: Element represents a category of a catalog of requirements.

elements.name: ResourceArchitecture
elements.notes: A type used to denote a model of the Architecture, described from the ResourcePerformer perspective.

elements.name: ResourceArtifact
elements.notes: A type of man-made object that contains no human beings (i.e. satellite, radio, petrol, gasoline, etc.).

elements.name: ResourceAsset
elements.notes: An abstract element used to group the elements of ResourcePerformer and DataElement allowing them to own DataRoles

elements.name: ResourceConstraint
elements.notes: A rule governing the structural or functional aspects of an implementation.

elements.name: ResourceInterface
elements.notes: A declaration that specifies a contract between the ResourcePerformers it is related to and any other ResourcePerformers it can interact with. It is also intended to be an implementation of a specification of an Interface in the Business and/or Service layer.

elements.name: ResourceMethod
elements.notes: A behavioral feature of a ResourcePerformer whose behavior is specified in a Function.

elements.name: ResourceMitigation
elements.notes: A set of measures intended to implement an OperationalMitigation. Comprises a subset of activities that are performed in mitigation of the risk to protect the asset that is the subject of risk (ResourceRole) at the physical level. In the case of a Risk applicable to security, the form of activity is a SecurityControl or an EnhancedSecurityControl, otherwise it is a Function.

elements.name: ResourceParameter
elements.notes: A type that represents inputs and outputs of an Function. It is typed by a ResourceInteractionItem.

elements.name: ResourcePerformer
elements.notes: An abstract grouping of elements that can perform Functions.

elements.name: ResourcePort
elements.notes: An interaction point for a ResourcePerformer through which it can interact with the outside environment and which is defined by a ResourceInterface.

elements.name: ResourceRole
elements.notes: Usage of a ResourcePerformer in the context of another ResourcePerformer. Creates a whole-part relationship.

elements.name: ResourceSignal
elements.notes: A property of an element representing something in the physical world, expressed in amounts of a unit of measure.

elements.name: ResourceSignalProperty
elements.notes: A property of an ResourceSignal typed by ResourceExchangeItem. It enables ResourceExchangeItem e.g. DataElement to be passed as arguments of the ResourceSignal.

elements.name: ResourceStateDescription
elements.notes: A state machine describing the behavior of a ResourcePerformer, depicting how the ResourcePerformer responds to various events and the actions.

elements.name: Responsibility
elements.notes: The type of duty required of a Person or Organization.

elements.name: Rule
elements.notes: An abstract type for all types of constraint (i.e. an OperationalConstraint could detail the rules of accountancy best practice).

elements.name: SecurityConstraint
elements.notes: A type of rule that captures a formal statement to define security laws, regulations, guidances, and policy. Element is not used in the current version of the framework and reserved for future developments.

elements.name: SecurityEnclave
elements.notes: Collection of information systems connected by one or more internal networks under the control of a single authority and security policy. The systems may be structured by physical proximity or by function, independent of location.  Element is not used in the current version of the framework and reserved for future developments.

elements.name: SecurityProcess
elements.notes: The security-related procedure that satisfies the security control requirement. Element is not used in the current version of the framework and reserved for future developments.

elements.name: ServiceFunction
elements.notes: An Activity that describes the abstract behavior of ServiceSpecifications, regardless of the actual implementation.

elements.name: ServiceFunctionAction
elements.notes: A call of a ServiceFunction in the context of another ServiceFunction.

elements.name: ServiceInterface
elements.notes: A contract that defines the ServiceMethods and ServiceMessageHandlers that the ServiceSpecification realizes.

elements.name: ServiceMethod
elements.notes: A behavioral feature of a ServiceSpecification whose behavior is specified in a ServiceFunction.

elements.name: ServiceParameter
elements.notes: A type that represents inputs and outputs of a ServiceFunction, represents inputs and outputs of a ServiceSpecification.

elements.name: ServicePolicy
elements.notes: A constraint governing the use of one or more ServiceSpecifications.

elements.name: ServicePort
elements.notes: An interaction point for a ServiceSpecification through which it can interact with the outside environment and which is defined by a ServiceInterface.

elements.name: ServiceSpecification
elements.notes: The specification of a set of functionality provided one element for the use of others.

elements.name: ServiceSpecificationRole
elements.notes: An assertion that a ServiceSecification calls upon another ServiceSpecification in order to deliver its stated functionality.

elements.name: ServiceStateDescription
elements.notes: A state machine descripting the behavior of a ServiceSpecification, depicting how the ServiceSpecification responds to various events and the actions.

elements.name: SMEReference
elements.notes: Element stands for a result of a workshop or expert knowledge.

elements.name: Software
elements.notes: A sub-type of ResourceArtifact that specifies an executable computer program.

elements.name: Standard
elements.notes: A ratified and peer-reviewed specification that is used to guide or constrain the architecture. A Standard may be applied to any element in the architecture.

elements.name: StandardOperationalActivity
elements.notes: A sub-type of OperationalActivity that is a standard operating procedure.

elements.name: StateDescription
elements.notes: An abstract type that represents a state machine (i.e. an OperationalStateDescription or ResourceStateDescription), depicting how the Asset responds to various events and the actions.

elements.name: StrategicConstraint
elements.notes: A Rule governing a capability.

elements.name: SubjectOfForecast
elements.notes: An abstract type grouping elements that can be the subject of a Forecast.

elements.name: SubOrganization
elements.notes: A type of a human being used to define the characteristics that need to be described for ActualPersons (e.g. properties such as address, telephone number, nationality, etc).

elements.name: System
elements.notes: An integrated set of elements, subsystems, or assemblies that accomplish a defined objective. These elements include products (hardware, software, firmware), processes, people, information, techniques, facilities, services, and other support elements (INCOSE SE Handbook V4, 2015).

elements.name: Technology
elements.notes: A sub type of ResourceArtifact that indicates a technology domain, i.e. nuclear, mechanical, electronic, mobile telephony etc.

elements.name: TemporalPart
elements.notes: A current or future state of the wholeLifeEnterprise or another EnterprisePhase.

elements.name: VersionOfConfiguration
elements.notes: A property of a WholeLifeConfiguration, used in version control of a VersionedElement. It asserts that a VersionedElement is a version of a WholeLifeConfiguration.

elements.name: View
elements.notes: An architecture view expresses the architecture of the system-of-interest in accordance with an architecture viewpoint (or simply, viewpoint). [ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2011(E)].

elements.name: Viewpoint
elements.notes: An architecture viewpoint frames (to formulate or construct in a particular style or language) one or more concerns. A concern can be framed by more than one viewpoint.  [ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2011(E)].

elements.name: WholeLifeConfiguration
elements.notes: A set of VersionedElements.

elements.name: WholeLifeEnterprise
elements.notes: A WholeLifeEnterprise is a purposeful endeavor of any size involving people, organizations and supporting systems. It is made up of TemporalParts and StructuralParts.

elements.name: A1 - Meta-Data Definitions
elements.notes: Architectures, particularly large ones, usually require meta-data tags to aid with searching and discovery.

elements.name: Meta-Data Definitions
elements.notes: Sicht A1 - Meta-Data Definitions.

elements.name: A2 - Architecture Products
elements.notes: The A2 Viewpoint specifies the structure of an architecture, and the products that describe the architecture. Each product may correspond to an architecture view. This viewpoint also traces the architectures onto the Enterprise Phases they correspond to (see also C2 – Enterprise Vision) and identifies the key stakeholders, their concerns and the products that address those concerns (from ISO/IEC/IEEE Standards).

elements.name: Architecture Products
elements.notes: Sicht A2 - Architecture Products.

elements.name: A3 - Architecture Correspondence
elements.notes: ISO/IEC/IEEE42010 introduces the idea of architecture correspondence and correspondence rules. Quoting from ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010; “A correspondence defines a relation between AD (Architecture Description) elements. Correspondences are used to express architecture relations of interest within an architecture description (or between architecture descriptions). Correspondences can be governed by correspondence rules. Correspondence rules are used to enforce relations within an architecture description (or between architecture descriptions).”

elements.name: Architecture Correspondence
elements.notes: Sicht A3 - Architecture Correspondence.

elements.name: A4 - Methodology Used
elements.notes: The A4 Viewpoint specifies the methodology used for the architecting activities. This methodology is described in NAFv4 Chapter 2. The content of the A4 viewpoint can also be modeled in the A1 viewpoint.

elements.name: Methodology Used
elements.notes: Sicht A4 - Methodology Used.

elements.name: A5 - Architecture Status
elements.notes: Since NAFv3.0, it has been possible to assign version numbers to views and specify their approval dates. In NAFv4.0, this is integrated with the meta-model’s generic project and milestone approach so that architecture releases are tracked against the architecture delivery project. The content of the A5 viewpoint can also be modeled in the A1 viewpoint.

elements.name: Architecture Status
elements.notes: Sicht A5 - Architecture Status.

elements.name: A6 - Architecture Version
elements.notes: Where the A5 Viewpoint shows the current version number and approval status for the architecture, the A6 Viewpoint shows the complete history of the architecture.

elements.name: Architecture Version
elements.notes: Sicht A6 - Architecture Version.

elements.name: A7 - Architecture Compliance
elements.notes: The A7 Viewpoint gives the overall specification of architecture meta-data.

elements.name: Architecture Compliance
elements.notes: Sicht A7 - Architecture Compliance.

elements.name: A8 - Standards
elements.notes: The A8 Viewpoint encompasses both technical and non-technical standards. The standards specified in the A8 view can be applied across the architecture to a variety of structural and behavioural elements. Standards are essential to the coherent running of businesses and to the delivery of reliable, interoperable systems.

elements.name: Standards
elements.notes: Sicht A8 - Standards.

elements.name: Ar - Architecture Roadmap
elements.notes: The Ar Viewpoint shows the history of the architecture project as well as its future direction.

elements.name: Architecture Roadmap
elements.notes: Sicht Ar - Architecture Roadmap.

elements.name: Business Process
elements.notes: Business Process

elements.name: Business Process
elements.notes: Sicht Business Process.

elements.name: C1 - Capability Taxonomy
elements.notes: The C1 Viewpoint specifies all the capabilities that are referenced throughout one or more architectures – i.e. one C1 may provide the definitive list of capabilities for a number of logical and resource architectures. The capabilities may be organised into specialisation hierarchies (taxonomies). Measures of Effectiveness (MoE) may be specified for each capability. Note that MoEs are inherited down a capability taxonomy.

elements.name: Capability Taxonomy
elements.notes: Sicht C1 - Capability Taxonomy.

elements.name: C1-S1 - Capability to Service Mapping
elements.notes: A C1-S1 Viewpoint presents a simple mapping of services to capabilities, showing which services contribute to which capability.

elements.name: Capability to Service Mapping
elements.notes: Sicht C1-S1 - Capability to Service Mapping.

elements.name: C2 - Enterprise Vision
elements.notes: The purpose of the C2 Viewpoint is to provide a strategic context for the capabilities described in the architecture and to specify the scope for the architecture. The C2 Viewpoint is high-level and describes the vision, goals, enduring tasks and capabilities using terminology that is easily understood by non-technical readers.

elements.name: Enterprise Vision
elements.notes: Sicht C2 - Enterprise Vision.

elements.name: C3 - Capability Dependencies
elements.notes: The C3 Viewpoint is intended to provide a means of analysing the dependencies between capabilities and between capability clusters. The composition of capabilities (into clusters) is logical and the purpose of the clusters is to guide enterprise management.

elements.name: Capability Dependencies
elements.notes: Sicht C3 - Capability Dependencies.

elements.name: C4 - Standard Processes
elements.notes: The C4 Viewpoint specifies Standard Operational Activities that can be re-used across multiple logical architectures (e.g. in L4, Logical Activities).

elements.name: Standard Processes
elements.notes: Sicht C4 - Standard Processes.

elements.name: C5 - Effects
elements.notes: The purpose of the C5 Viewpoint is to describe the operational effect of the capabilities, activities and services according to the expected goals. The C5 Viewpoint is high-level description that should be easily understood by non-technical readers.

elements.name: Effects
elements.notes: Sicht C5 - Effects.

elements.name: C7 - Performance Parameters
elements.notes: In the C7 Viewpoint the capability requirements (and existing capabilities) can be expressed in terms of Measures of Effectiveness (MoEs). These are high-level metrics used to judge the level of capability.

elements.name: Performance Parameters
elements.notes: Sicht C7 - Performance Parameters.

elements.name: C8 - Planning Assumptions
elements.notes: The C8 Viewpoint is concerned with identification and description of assumptions that have been made for the implementation of capabilities. Assumptions can be expressed by means of requirements.

elements.name: Planning Assumptions
elements.notes: Sicht C8 - Planning Assumptions.

elements.name: Cr - Capability Roadmap
elements.notes: The Cr Viewpont supports the Capability Audit process by providing a method to identify gaps or duplications in capability provision. Cr indicates capability increments, which are derived from delivery milestones within acquisition projects.

elements.name: Capability Roadmap
elements.notes: Sicht Cr - Capability Roadmap.

elements.name: L1 - Node Types
elements.notes: The L1 Viewpoint defines all of the Nodes that will appear in a Logical Architecture. Nodes are elements of capability assembled and orchestrated in the Logical Architecture (see L2 - Logical Scenario and L4 - Logical Activities views). The levels of capability provided by each node are expressed as Measures of Performance (MoPs) and these may be dependent on the environments in which the Node is required to operate.

elements.name: Node Types
elements.notes: Sicht L1 - Node Types.

elements.name: L2 - Logical Scenario
elements.notes: The L2 Viewpoint specifies Nodes (elements of capability) in context of each other. The context is usually expressed in terms of the information that flows between the nodes (e.g. the information flow requirements between capabilities in a given scenario) but may also be flows of materiel, human resource or energy.

elements.name: Logical Scenario
elements.notes: Sicht L2 - Logical Scenario.

elements.name: L2-L3 - Logical Concept
elements.notes: The L2-L3 Viewpoint is concerned with providing an executive level, scenario-based communication of the architecture purpose, scope and content.

elements.name: Logical Concept
elements.notes: Sicht L2-L3 - Logical Concept.

elements.name: L3 - Node Interactions
elements.notes: L3 is used to provide further detail of the interoperability requirements associated with the operational capability of interest. The focus is on logical flows that cross the capability boundary. Although the primary purpose of the L3 Viewpoint is to specify information exchanges, the L3 may also list flows of materiel, energy and human resources.

elements.name: Node Interactions
elements.notes: Sicht L3 - Node Interactions.

elements.name: L4 - Logical Activities
elements.notes: The L4 Viewpoint describes the operational activities that are being conducted within the mission or scenario. These activities are defined at a logical, solution-neutral level so as to enable different solutions in the physical layer. The L4 Viewpoint describes the activities associated with the logical architecture, as well as the:

elements.name: Logical Activities
elements.notes: Sicht L4 - Logical Activities.

elements.name: L4-P4 - Activity To Function Mapping
elements.notes: The L4-P4 Viewpoint depicts the mapping of Resource Functions (and optionally, the resources that provide them) to operational activities and/or service functions. For operational activities it thus identifies the transformation of an operational need into a purposeful action performed by a system or solution. For service functions it provides the link between the services used at the operational level and the specific Resource Functions provided by the resources supporting the services.

elements.name: Activity To Function Mapping
elements.notes: Sicht L4-P4 - Activity To Function Mapping.

elements.name: L5 - Logical States
elements.notes: The L5 Viewpoint specifies the typical states a node may have and the possible transitions between those states (i.e. changes of state). Triggers for state changes may also be defined. Actions may be associated with a given state or with the transition between states in response to stimuli (e.g. triggers and events).

elements.name: Logical States
elements.notes: Sicht L5 - Logical States.

elements.name: L6 - Logical Sequence
elements.notes: Operational Event-Trace Descriptions, sometimes called sequence diagrams, event scenarios or timing diagrams, allow the tracing of interactions between nodes in a scenario or critical sequence of events. The node interactions usually correspond to flows of information but may describe flows of energy, materiel or people specified in the L2, Logical Scenario.

elements.name: Logical Sequence
elements.notes: Sicht L6 - Logical Sequence.

elements.name: L7 - Information Model
elements.notes: The L7 Viewpoint is used to document the business information. It describes the information that can be exchanged along the logical flows in the architecture, specified in L3 Node Interactions.

elements.name: Information Model
elements.notes: Sicht L7 - Information Model.

elements.name: L8 - Logical Constraints
elements.notes: The L8 Viewpoint is used to constrain the logical architecture without forcing a particular solution. L8 is used for rules which are not expressed as behavioural models, interactions or measures of effectiveness, i.e. they are textual statements of requirements that constrain the architecture.

elements.name: Logical Constraints
elements.notes: Sicht L8 - Logical Constraints.

elements.name: Lr - Lines of Development
elements.notes: The Lr Viewpoint is primarily intended to support the acquisition process across multiple projects or programmes, highlighting dependencies the logical dependencies between capabilities, projects and the integration of all lines of development to achieve a successfully integrated military capability. Use of the Lr Viewpoint should support the management of capability delivery and be aligned with Cr, Capability Roadmap.

elements.name: Lines of Development
elements.notes: Sicht Lr - Lines of Development.

elements.name: P1 - Resource Types
elements.notes: The P1 Viewpoint collects together all the Resource Types in the architecture together with a depiction of their performance characteristics. P1 also provides a summary of the technologies and competencies that impact on the Resources that constitute the architecture.

elements.name: Resource Types
elements.notes: Sicht P1 - Resource Types.

elements.name: P2 - Resource Structure
elements.notes: The P2 Viewpoint links together the operational and physical architecture viewpoints by depicting how types of Resource are structured and interact to realize the logical architecture specified in L2, Logical Scenario. The P2 Viewpoint may represent the realization of a requirement specified in a L2 (i.e. in a “to-be” architecture) and so there may be many alternative Resource viewpoint suites that could realize the operational requirement. Alternatively, in an “as-is” architecture, a L2 may just be a simplified, logical representation of the P2 Viewpoint to allow communication of key information flows to non-technical stakeholders.

elements.name: Resource Structure
elements.notes: Sicht P2 - Resource Structure.

elements.name: P3 - Resource Connectivity
elements.notes: The networks and pathways documented in a P3 Viewpoint represent the physical implementation of the logical flows identified in a L2, Logical Scenario, or L3, Node Interactions View.

elements.name: Resource Connectivity
elements.notes: Sicht P3 - Resource Connectivity.

elements.name: P4 - Resource Functions
elements.notes: The Functionality Description provides detailed information regarding the allocation of functions to resources, and flows between Resource Functions. The P4 Viewpoint is the Physical Resource counterpart to the L4 Logical Activities Viewpoint.

elements.name: Resource Functions
elements.notes: Sicht P4 - Resource Functions.

elements.name: P5 - Resource States
elements.notes: The P5 Viewpoint identifies the states a Resource can be, the allowable changes between those states, and the stimuli (e.g. triggers and events) that cause the state changes.

elements.name: Resource States
elements.notes: Sicht P5 - Resource States.

elements.name: P6 - Resource Sequence
elements.notes: The P6 Viewpoint is valuable for moving to the next level of detail from the initial solution design, to help define a sequence of functions and Resource Interactions, and to ensure that each participating Resource or Port has the necessary information, at the right time, in order to perform its assigned functionality.

elements.name: Resource Sequence
elements.notes: Sicht P6 - Resource Sequence.

elements.name: P7 - Data Model
elements.notes: The P7 Viewpoint is one of the architectural products closest to actual system design in the NAF. It is used to describe how the information represented in the L7 Logical Data Model Viewpoint is implemented.

elements.name: Data Model
elements.notes: Sicht P7 - Data Model.

elements.name: P8 - Resource Constraints
elements.notes: The P8 Viewpoint describes constraints on the Resources, Resource Functions, data and communications that make up a Physical Architecture.

elements.name: Resource Constraints
elements.notes: Sicht P8 - Resource Constraints.

elements.name: Pr - Configuration Management
elements.notes: The Pr Viewpoint provides an overview of how Resource Assets change over time (note that NAF v3.1 only allowed for Capability Configurations whereas now this is opened up to all Resource Types). It shows the structure of different versions of Resource Assets (usually Capability Configurations or Service Implementations) mapped against a timeline.

elements.name: Configuration Management
elements.notes: Sicht Pr - Configuration Management.

elements.name: R2 - Requirement Catalogue
elements.notes: The R2 represents a catalog of requirements in the architectural model. For this purpose, categories can be created in which the functional and non-functional requirements can be grouped.

elements.name: Requirement Catalogue
elements.notes: Sicht R2 - Requirement Catalogue.

elements.name: R3 - Requirement Dependencies
elements.notes: The R3 is used to show dependencies between different requirements.

elements.name: Requirement Dependencies
elements.notes: Sicht R3 - Requirement Dependencies.

elements.name: R7 - Requirement Derivation
elements.notes: The R7 assigns functional and non-functional requirements to the demanding architectural elements. In addition, information about the planned realization can be shown.

elements.name: Requirement Derivation
elements.notes: Sicht R7 - Requirement Derivation.

elements.name: R8 - Requirement Fulfilment
elements.notes: The R8 is used to determine and map acceptance and evaluation criteria for the individual functional and non-functional requirements.

elements.name: Requirement Fulfilment
elements.notes: Sicht R8 - Requirement Fulfilment.

elements.name: Rr - Requirement Realization
elements.notes: In the Rr, requirements are assigned to the realizing architectural elements.

elements.name: Requirement Realization
elements.notes: Sicht Rr - Requirement Realization.

elements.name: S1 - Service Taxonomy
elements.notes: The purpose of the S1 Viewpoint is to provide a governance structure for a Service-Oriented Architecture. Along with S3, Service Interfaces, it specifies a standard library of service specifications for an enterprise, to which service implementers are expected to conform.

elements.name: Service Taxonomy
elements.notes: Sicht S1 - Service Taxonomy.

elements.name: S2 - Service Structure
elements.notes: The S2 Viewpoint is concerned with identification and description of how services are structured to create a higher-aggregated service. To provide highlevel views, dependencies to other services, nodes and resources as well as service interfaces and service functions can be represented.

elements.name: Service Structure
elements.notes: Sicht S2 - Service Structure.

elements.name: S3 - Service Interfaces
elements.notes: The S3 Viewpoint is concerned with the identification and definition of service interfaces.

elements.name: Service Interfaces
elements.notes: Sicht S3 - Service Interfaces.

elements.name: S4 - Service Functions
elements.notes: The S4 Viewpoint is the key behavioural specification for services. Equivalent in nature to L4, Logical Activities and P4, Resources Functions, it specifies a set of functions that a service implementation is expected to perform. Implementation of that behaviour is represented in P4, Resource Functions, and L4-P4, Activity to Function Mapping.

elements.name: Service Functions
elements.notes: Sicht S4 - Service Functions.

elements.name: S5 - Service States
elements.notes: The S5 Viewpoint is a specification of the allowable states of a service, and the possible transitions between them. This specification constrains how implementations of the service will behave.  It is, though, generally considered a good practice to make services stateless - i.e. consumers of a service are not aware of what state the service is in.

elements.name: Service States
elements.notes: Sicht S5 - Service States.

elements.name: S6 - Service Interactions
elements.notes: Service Interaction Descriptions, sometimes called sequence diagrams, event scenarios or timing diagrams, allow the tracing of interactions between services in a composition or critical sequence of events.

elements.name: Service Interactions
elements.notes: Sicht S6 - Service Interactions.

elements.name: S7 - Service Interface Parameters
elements.notes: Specifies the interfaces that a service provides and uses, defines which services are compatible with which other services.

elements.name: Service Interface Parameters
elements.notes: Sicht S7 - Service Interface Parameters.

elements.name: S8 - Service Policy
elements.notes: The S8 Viewpoint specifies constraints against services to which implementations must conform.

elements.name: Service Policy
elements.notes: Sicht S8 - Service Policy.

elements.name: Sr - Service Roadmap
elements.notes: The Sr Viewpoint supports the Service Audit process by providing a method to identify gaps or duplications in service provision. Sr indicates service lifetime evolutions, which are derived from delivery milestones within acquisition projects.

elements.name: Service Roadmap
elements.notes: Sicht Sr - Service Roadmap.

elements.name: Projektarchitektur
elements.notes: Abkuerzung fuer das Projekt Projektarchitektur.

packages.notes: Je Element-Stereotyp ein Paket mit dessen Definition.
